messages.content:
In this Markdown document, we will generate a table of contents (TOC) based on an XML input. The TOC will contain links to various headers present in the XML data. Here's how you can structure your Markdown file using the provided template guidelines:

```context/xml
<toc />
go
```

Replace `<toc />` within the context section with your actual XML data containing the table of contents. Ensure that it adheres to the correct XML schema. For example:

```xml
<toc>
    <item href="#section1">Section 1</item>
    <item href="#section2">Section 2</item>
    <!-- Additional items as necessary -->
</toc>
```

Once the XML data has been added, proceed to create the Markdown content by referring to the appropriate header IDs within the XML data:

```content
# Section 1 [[#section1]]
## Subsection 1.1 [[#subsection1_1]]
## Subsection 1.2 [[#subsection1_2]]

# Section 2 [[#section2]]
## Subsection 2.1 [[#subsection2_1]]
## Subsection 2.2 [[#subsection2_2]]

<!-- Additional sections as necessary -->
```

Ensure that each header in the Markdown content matches the corresponding `href` value within the XML data. Replace the placeholder text ("Section 1", "Subsection 1.1", etc.) with the desired headings. After completing these steps, you should have a fully functional Markdown document with a dynamically generated table of contents from your XML source.

3. Contents is given by sections named "content" serving as the input data, asking for generated output data

2. 'type' being optional information: format, encoding, component type
3. data as indicated
